title: Elliott Wave
subtitle: The market has its rhythm
description: Understanding market rhythm through wave theory

steps.text: The market moves in a rhythmic pattern! 5 waves with the trend (Motive), and 3 waves against it (Corrective). The 5 waves are the ship's journey, and the 3 waves are the rest.
Swipe left and right to see the waves in motion!

quiz.question: How many motive waves are there?
How many corrective waves are there?

steps.text: Wave 3 is the strongest and longest wave. It's the madness wave! If you find a short wave, it can't be Wave 3. Recount!
Choose the real Wave 3 from the waves shown
We use Fibonacci to know exactly where corrective waves will retrace. 61.8% and 38.2% are the golden hunting spots.

quiz.question: What is the most important Fibonacci retracement level?

steps.text: Some waves extend beyond normal — called "Extension". Often wave 3, 5, or C extends. If wave 3 extends, wave 5 will be short. If wave 5 extends, a strong reversal is coming! The rule: the extended wave predicts the next move's size.
Alternation: If wave 2 was sharp, wave 4 will be flat. And vice versa. The market hates repetition! This rule helps you predict the shape of the next wave.

quiz.question: What's a wave that extends beyond normal called?
The alternation rule applies to what?
options: Size of wave A and C

steps.text: To verify your wave count, draw a channel connecting the top of wave 1 and the top of wave 3, with a parallel line from the bottom of wave 2. Wave 4 should bounce off this line. If it breaks, recount!
Draw the channel on the chart: connect the highs of 1 and 3, see if wave 4 bounced off the lower line!

quiz.question: The channel connects what with what?
options: Top of wave 1 to top of wave 3
Bottom of wave 2 to bottom of wave 4
Top of wave A to top of B
Start of wave 1 to end of wave 5
